thread:
leo: FYI ran into a blocker with the Go sample during onboarding. The UI does a whoami call to show org/name, but the Go SDK doesn't expose that route. REST works.

maya: which route? `/v1/admin/me` again?

leo: yup. curl with token returns 200 and user JSON. Go client has no Admin() accessor. Using client.Admin().Me() panics: undefined method.

ci-bot: created issue RED-GB-203 in go-sdk repo: missing admin/me binding. https://git.redwood/dev/go-sdk/issues/203 :ticket:

frank: can you paste the sampleapp snippet? curious if the app treats absence as a 404 or error.

leo: sampleapp snippet below — it retries on non-2xx and we ended up with sidekiq jobs piling up:

```
// onboard.go
c := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_TOKEN"))
me, err := c.Admin().Me()
if err != nil {
  log.Printf("onboard: admin.me failed: %v", err)
  return err // job retried many times
}
openProfile(me)
```

maya: interesting. In our generated bindings the admin tag is present in the OpenAPI, but Go codegen omitted it because the package name collides with an internal `admin` package. We could generate it as `adminv1` or expose a getter `AdminClient()` instead.

tess: separate issue: we also saw the Go HTTP layer lowercasing all headers for canonicalization. On-prem proxies with strict plugins treat `authorization` (lowercase) as different from `Authorization` and return 401. So in some installs users get 401s while others are fine.

leo: exact symptom: in staging the sampleapp keeps getting 401s intermittently, rotates token, then eventually a request succeeds and onboarding continues. Combined with missing Admin binding it produced a long onboarding delay.

ci-bot: triage: labels `sdk/go`, `bug`, `onboarding`. Assigned to @maya. Priority set to P1.

maya: plan: 1) quick patch to codegen to emit `AdminClient()` and a convenience `Admin()` method. 2) stop lowercasing header keys in the transport layer (preserve original header case). 3) add an integration test hitting `/v1/admin/me` against the staging proxy.

frank: can we also update the Go sampleapp README with a temp workaround to call REST directly using net/http? saves folks from being blocked.

leo: will add a note and the curl snippet. also adding a one-liner REST fallback in the sampleapp to avoid retries piling up: if SDK accessor missing, call REST and short-circuit retries.

maya: ETA: patch branch today, cut a patch release tomorrow if tests pass. I'll drop a link here when the PR is up.

leo: appreciated. tagging this as a docs + SDK backlog item so it doesn't regress for private deployments. :+1:
